A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVLift research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting a reliable comparison. All 11 pages of each were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-lifting experiments on five datasets, ablations in Table 3, and human perceptual-study results in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original five-dataset experiments, ablation results, and human perceptual study in Tables 1–3 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same four stages: line-conditioned diffusion, multi-view optimization, synthetic multi-view data generation, and multi-view diffusion with cross-view attention. The objectives and reconstruction procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIST++, Steezy, NicoleMove, CatPlay, and OMOMO for the same human, animal, and human-object interaction tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MotionBERT, WHAM, ElePose, SMPLify, and MAS for human motion; MAS and adapted SMPLify for animals; and adapted SMPLify for interactions. Comparator membership and adaptations are unchanged.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, single-view training setup, evaluation metrics, OMOMO largebox subset, and testing procedures are unchanged. The perceptual study still selects 15 sequences per approach for each of the three human-motion datasets.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 3 retain the same stage comparisons, direct-3D SDS alternative, and unconditional-prior variant. The qualitative analyses of human motion, animal motion, and interactions are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and preference percentages. Neither adds or removes seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 5, and the qualitative comparisons retain their results. For example, MVLift's AIST++ root translation error, MPJPE, and PA-MPJPE remain 67.6, 110.7, and 79.2, respectively, under the same reported settings.

T1.justification: The epipolar geometry definitions and Equations (1)–(6), including the diffusion, line-matching, SDS, and multi-view consistency formulations, are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of global 3D motion estimation using only 2D training sequences, progressive multi-view consistency, and generalization across human, animal, and interaction domains. The five-dataset performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of baseline failures through depth ambiguity, restricted training distributions, and insufficient multi-view consistency remain unchanged. The rationale for the successive stages is retained, without new limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The camera arrangements, pose-extraction procedures, transformer details, SMPL/VPoser fitting, and baseline implementation descriptions are unchanged. No new hyperparameters, resource information, or code/data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 retains the same research positioning, and the bibliography retains the same 67 numbered references. Shortened venue names and omitted bibliographic page ranges do not change the cited works or their relationship to MVLift.

P1.justification: Figure 1's caption receives light wording edits, such as replacing 'Our MVLift' with 'Our framework, MVLift.' Reference formatting is standardized and shortened, while the main narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 uses higher-resolution image assets, and Figure 3 has small typography and spacing changes. Page-number footers are removed and the shortened bibliography reflows. All seven figures and three tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 provides modest visual and editorial polish, particularly in Figures 1 and 3 and the bibliography. The earlier figures were already interpretable, while the scientific explanation, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These refinements do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or decline.
